quotes.text: Set up a subscription with local South Korean cards
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: You must convert your prices to KRW to use the payment method.
Set the value of the `default_payment_method` parameter to the PaymentMethod ID from the SetupIntent response.
Set the `payment_settings.save_default_payment_method=on_subscription` parameter to save a payment method when a subscription is activated.

findings: The same URL's November capture contains only title and three variant links (new 5-13), replacing a May capture that rendered all three detailed variants (old 4-214). This is an upstream variant-index rendering change. It does not establish removal, deprecation, changed eligibility, or changed behavior for SetupIntents, Subscriptions API, or hosted Checkout. The new index is navigation-only and should not be added as a factual raw_files source.

The May SetupIntents variant creates/confirms a SetupIntent to save a payment method, passes its client_secret to Stripe.js for local-processor authorization, then creates a subscription with the resulting default_payment_method (old 8-56). Its example includes usage=off_session, mandate_data, and subscription off_session:true (old 38-72), but the captured prose does not call all example fields universal requirements. The current source lines 19-20 make that unsupported leap.

The May SetupIntents variant contains a prose inconsistency: its opening claims the first call creates a Subscription and PaymentIntent (old 12), whereas the actual heading, command and following explanation create a SetupIntent before the subscription call (old 34-56). Summarize the concrete path with the inconsistency noted, rather than treating the opening sentence as a proven sequence.

The May Subscriptions API variant creates a subscription with payment_behavior=default_incomplete and save_default_payment_method=on_subscription in the shown example, expands latest_invoice.payments and confirmation_secret, then confirms a PaymentIntent; requires_action means local-processor authentication remains (old 115-156). Do not collapse this path into the SetupIntent path or infer payment success from requires_action.

The May hosted Checkout variant asks the customer to authorize future use, creates a subscription-mode Checkout Session with card and kr_card in the sample, and tests a successful redirect/authentication transition from requires_action to succeeded (old 158-214). The 100,000 KRW monthly price is explicitly a stock-photo-service example (old 168-180), while the SetupIntents section states KRW conversion for the method (old 32).

May confirmation prose says set payment_method_types to kr_card in both direct-confirm paths (old 79, 143), but the SetupIntents confirm command instead contains payment_method_data[]=type and payment_method_data[]=kr_card (old 81-87), and the Subscriptions confirm command sets payment_method_data[type]=kr_card with mandate_data (old 145-154). These snippets cannot establish a single required confirmation parameter; preserve the discrepancy as a source warning.

Current source line 13 claims 'same structure as Revolut Pay' without support in either assigned capture, and line 20 says mandate_data required without limiting it to the depicted calls. The concept's source route at wiki/concepts/stripe-korea-payment-methods.md:141 repeats the blanket off_session+mandate_data requirement. A narrow correction is warranted despite no substantive November behavior update.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May's three integration variants and their distinct examples as dated 2026-05-13 evidence (old 8-89, 91-156, 158-214); November's index-only capture supplies routing, not replacement behavioral evidence (new 9-13).

Preserve the May KRW requirement from the SetupIntents section and its successful-payment/active outcome qualification, without promoting the example's 100,000 KRW amount or every command parameter to universal requirements (old 18-32, 75-89, 168-180).

Retain the May source's client/server separation and local processor authentication boundary: server creates/sets up objects, Stripe.js client redirect authorizes the mandate, and requires_action is not payment success (old 34-52, 77-89, 115-156).
conflicts: Current source lines 19-20 and wiki/concepts/stripe-korea-payment-methods.md:141 say off_session=true and mandate_data are required generally. Old raw shows them in path-specific examples only (old 38-49, 63-72, 145-154), and hosted Checkout's sample lacks those parameters (old 199-210). Narrow to the depicted paths; the November index cannot arbitrate API requiredness.

Old raw line 12 describes a first Subscriptions API call in the SetupIntents section, while old lines 34-56 show an initial SetupIntent call. Old raw lines 79/143 also name payment_method_types in prose while their respective confirm commands use payment_method_data fields (old 81-87, 145-154). Do not silently resolve either discrepancy into a new behavioral rule.

Current source line 13 says 'same structure as Revolut Pay' but that comparison is unsupported by the assigned KR card captures. Remove or separately source it; it is not evidence of interchangeable payment-method requirements.

Current source line 36 presents SetupIntent succeeded before subscription creation as an unconditional transition, while old raw lines 52-56 explain client redirect and later subscription creation without an explicit SetupIntent status guarantee in this passage. Preserve the redirect and authorization step without inventing that status outcome.
unresolved_questions: The navigation-only November capture does not show the current contents of its three query-parameter variant targets. Their current instructions and eligibility need separately pinned variant captures before updating behavior claims.

The old SetupIntents opening/steps and payment_method_types prose versus command discrepancies remain unresolved within the pinned old capture; this review cannot decide exact API requiredness from examples alone.
The capture does not verify live account eligibility, local-processor authentication completion, recurring payment success, or that every South Korean method shares these parameters.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/kr-card, the 2026-11-07 capture is a thirteen-line variant index that directs readers to SetupIntents, Subscriptions API and Stripe-hosted Checkout pages (new lines 5-13). It contains no substantive integration instructions. The May capture documents those three paths with KRW pricing, local-processor authentication, distinct server SetupIntent/subscription and PaymentIntent-confirmation steps, and a hosted Checkout example (old lines 8-89, 91-156, 158-214). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-kr-card]] accurately routes to the three historical paths but overstates example fields as universal requirements (source 19-20). The May SetupIntents opening also conflicts with its own SetupIntent steps (old 12 versus 34-56).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/kr-card, the visible change is presentational routing: November lists three query-parameter variants (new lines 9-13) where May rendered all three flows together (old lines 8-214). This does not prove deprecation, removal, changed availability, or a replacement API behavior. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-kr-card]] should preserve May KRW and authentication facts as dated evidence (old 32, 52, 89, 156), narrow its off_session and mandate_data 'required' claims (source 19-20), and flag the May prose/command conflict: payment_method_types is named in prose but confirmation examples use payment_method_data (old 79-87, 143-154). The reciprocal [[stripe-korea-payment-methods]] source route at concept line 141 repeats the overbroad requirement. Example 100,000 KRW pricing and requires_action are not payment-finality or universal-parameter proofs.
